headings.title: SMTO-GWT-0089 — The Gateway's data is in use or the Gateway is shutting down

html:
SMTO-GWT-0089 — The Gateway's data is in use or the Gateway is shutting down

GUID: cdf2434f-3ec2-5ed8-8303-6df3c2a840ae
Slug: gateway-state-owner-unavailable
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • Only one copy of the Gateway may use its data folder at a time. Another copy is using it, or the Gateway is still shutting down, so this one can't take new work or start.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a minute if the Gateway was just restarted, updated or stopped, then select Check connection in Settings › Setup › Gateways. A Gateway that is shutting down refuses new work until it has finished saving.
  2. On the Gateway computer, make sure only one copy of the Gateway is running, including any copy started automatically when the computer starts. Two copies sharing one data folder could both run the same job, so the second one is refused.
  3. If someone is backing up or repairing the Gateway's data, wait until all its jobs have finished before trying again. Backup and repair refuse to run while any job from that Gateway is still active.

What success looks like

  • One Gateway is running and shows as connected in Settings › Setup › Gateways, and new requests start normally.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't delete lock files or the data folder to force it to start.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway could not establish exclusive ownership of its state: another process holds the owner lock, the owner is draining or not ready, a forked child tried to use it, workers were still live during backup or repair, or recovery bindings changed after startup.

What this means

  • Gateway state access could not establish exclusive local ownership, encountered a draining or non-ready lifecycle, a foreign directory owner, live workers during maintenance or recovery imports changed after initialization. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway state access could not establish exclusive local ownership, encountered a draining or non-ready lifecycle, a foreign directory owner, live workers during maintenance or recovery imports changed after initialization.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the owner/lifecycle or configuration failure and inspect original worker identities before maintenance; never infer that a PID alone authorizes taking over state.

How to fix it

  • Read the message ("Gateway state already has an owner", "Gateway owner is still draining", "Gateway is quiescing", "Gateway workers must finish before backup or repair", "Gateway state is in use"). Ensure exactly one Gateway process (including any service manager auto-restart) uses this GATEWAY_JOB_DIR/GATEWAY_TLS_STATE_DIR, let the draining owner finish shutdown and its workers exit, then start one Gateway with the complete configuration. Do not delete .owner.lock or .runtime.lock files.
  • Use the owning Gateway's shutdown and drain controls, correct the indicated ownership or startup configuration, and start one legitimate owner after retained workers settle.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • One legitimate owner starts with complete configuration after previous work and shutdown are reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
